Let $W$ be a finite unconstrained DMC from finite nonempty $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$, with rates and logarithms in nats. The one-letter function $E_0(\rho,P)$ for $\rho\ge0$ and $E_{0x}(\rho,P)$ for $\rho\ge1$ are defined in [[def-it-one-letter-gallager-exponent-functions]]. Their maxima over the input simplex are attained and finite by [[lem-it-gallager-input-maxima-attained]]. For every $\rho\ge0$, define $E_0(\rho):=\max_P E_0(\rho,P)$; on the random-coding range set
$$E_r(R):=\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}\{E_0(\rho)-\rho R\}.$$
The expurgated function and sphere-packing expression are
$$E_{\rm ex}(R):=\sup_{\rho\ge1}\left\{\max_P E_{0x}(\rho,P)-\rho R\right\},\qquad E_{\rm sp}(R):=\sup_{\rho\ge0}\{E_0(\rho)-\rho R\}.$$
These functions define lower or upper bounds used on this page; they do not assert that an error-exponent limit exists or that the sphere-packing bound applies without its later strict-feasibility hypothesis.

actual_direct_use_quotes:
For a finite DMC $W$, the functions $P\mapsto E_0(\rho,P)$ for each $\rho\ge0$ and $P\mapsto E_{0x}(\rho,P)$ for each $\rho\ge1$, defined in [[def-it-one-letter-gallager-exponent-functions]], are finite and continuous on the input probability simplex. Consequently, each attains a finite maximum there. At $\rho=0$, $E_0(0,P)=0$ for every $P$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite DMC $W$, its finite nonempty alphabets, a real $\rho$ in one of the stated ranges, and an input law $P$.

[F1] [[def-it-one-letter-gallager-exponent-functions]]: for $\rho\ge0$, $E_0$ is the negative logarithm of the finite sum of powers $1/(1+\rho)$ and $1+\rho$; for $\rho\ge1$, $E_{0x}$ is $-\rho$ times the logarithm of the finite sum of $P(x)P(x')B(x,x')^{1/\rho}$, with $0^a=0$ for $a>0$.

[F2] [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]]: each row $W(\cdot\mid x)$ is a probability vector.

[F3] [[def-real-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], and [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]: $t^a$ is continuous for $t>0$ when $a$ is fixed, $0^a=0$ for $a>0$, and $\ln$ and $\exp$ are strictly increasing inverses.

## Proof

1.1 For fixed distinct codewords $x^n,x'^n$, if ML decoding chooses the competitor when $x^n$ was sent, then $W^n(y^n\mid x'^n)\ge W^n(y^n\mid x^n)$. On that event $W^n(y^n\mid x^n)\le\sqrt{W^n(y^n\mid x^n)W^n(y^n\mid x'^n)}.$ Summing over outputs and using a union bound over competitors gives message error at most $f_m:=\sum_{j\ne m}B^n(x_m^n,x_j^n)$, where $B^n(x^n,x'^n)=\prod_iB(x_i,x'_i)$.
